question.problem:
$$
⟨\,\sqrt{z-1}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,,\,\sqrt{z-1}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,,\,\text{_______}⟩
$$

 

The fundamental vector product of the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $y=\sqrt{z-1}$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $z$-axis for $z\in [1,10]$ is given above. What is the $3$rd component of the product?
question.worked_solution:
Notice that $y=\sqrt{z-1}\ge 0$ for all $z\in [1,10].$ The parametrization of our surface of revolution is  

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(z)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,f(z)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩,\,(z,\theta )\in D\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(z)=\sqrt{z-1},$ and  

$$
D=\{(z,\theta )\,:\,1\le z\le 10,\,0\le \theta <2\pi \}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{z}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂z},\,\frac{∂y}{∂z},\,\frac{∂z}{∂z}⟩=⟨{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂y}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂z}{∂\theta }⟩=⟨f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-{f}^{′}f{sin}^{2}⁡\theta -{f}^{′}f{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-{f}^{′}f⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f=\sqrt{z-1},$ we obtain ${f}^{′}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{z-1}}.$ So, finally, we conclude that the fundamental vector product is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}=⟨\sqrt{z-1}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\sqrt{z-1}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-\frac{1}{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
